- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.33), model often underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment history shows repeated alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.33/1.00/0.33), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward historical 30-day average for next 2–3 periods.
- For horizon >10 days, model tends to overreact to sentiment; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility in forecast.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.33) or erratic, model underperforms in late periods; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 3–5 days of horizon.
